html:
The battle, around 1235, in which the Mandinka prince Sundiata Keita defeated Sumanguru Kanté, king of Sosso. It is remembered as the founding moment of the Mali Empire.

After the power of Ghana faded, the kingdom of Sosso rose in the region and took over the small Mande chiefdoms of the upper Niger. Its king, Sumanguru, was a blacksmith, feared as a sorcerer. The Mande clans united behind Sundiata, who had grown up in exile, and he led their armies against Sosso.

The exact date and place are uncertain; Kirina lies near the Niger, not far from modern Bamako. What we know of the battle comes mostly from the Epic of Sundiata. In it, the fight is as much magic as war. Sundiata's sister learns the secret of Sumanguru's power, and Sundiata shoots him with an arrow tipped with the spur of a white rooster. His magic broken, Sumanguru flees into the hills and vanishes.

After Kirina, Sundiata took over the lands of Sosso and built a new empire that would control the gold fields and the trade across the Sahara.
